newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Solarz arrives in Cambodia for talks with Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Solarz arrives in Cambodia for talks with Hun Sen.

text.p: The U.S. special envoy on Cambodia arrived in Phnom Penh on Thursday for talks with strongman Hun Sen aimed at resolving the country's political crisis.

Stephen Solarz did not speak to reporters at Phnom Penh airport but in Bangkok earlier in the day he applauded Hun Sen's decision to allow the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to play a role in trying to resolve the Cambodian turmoil.

"We are encouraged by what now appears to be a willingness on the part of Hun Sen to accept the ASEAN offer to use its good offices to facilitate a political resolution of the Cambodian crisis," Solarz told reporters after meeting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
Solarz was due to meet Hun Sen for talks on Friday morning, U.S. officials said.
Solarz, who is on a whirlwind diplomatic tour of Asian capitals seeking a solution to the turmoil in Cambodia, said the United States hoped to work closely with ASEAN to try end the problem.

Cambodia had been expected to join ASEAN on Wednesday, but Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh led the regional organisation to postpone Cambodia's admission to the group indefinitely.

Hun Sen had originally rejected ASEAN's efforts to mediate and help find a political solution to the crisis. He told a group of ASEAN foreign ministers in Phnom Penh on the weekend that he did not want their intervention.
But in a suprise change of position Hun Sen told reporters on Thursday that ASEAN's role in ensuring Cambodia's stability was needed.
"The stability of Cambodia -- we need the role of ASEAN," he said.
Hun Sen also said he was not upset by ASEAN's decision to delay Cambodia's membership.
"I don't feel any upset because of that ... we have to respect the decision made by ASEAN," Hun Sen told reporters.
"We're waiting for ASEAN's decision next time," he said.
Burma and Laos became full ASEAN members on Wednesday, joining Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, in the grouping.
ASEAN was preparing fresh proposals for Hun Sen on Thursday in an attempt to mediate the conflict in Cambodia, officials in Kuala Lumpur said.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who has been involved in brokering Cambodian diplomacy for years, said he and two other ASEAN ministers discussed the ideas with Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot on Wednesday.
"The three ministers will try to pick up the thread where we left it and continue our efforts," he told Reuters on Thursday.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright, speaking in Los Angelese on Wednesday, pledged that the United States would do all it could to see that Hun Sen made good on promises to accept mediation.

Solarz met Ranariddh in Bangkok earlier on Thursday and was due to travel to Kuala Lumpur after his talks with Hun Sen on Friday and report to Albright, the U.S. embassy in the Malaysian capital said.

Albright and 10 other foreign ministers from Western and Asian powers will attend a weekend meeting with their ASEAN counterparts at the ASEAN Regional Forum, Asia's premier conference on security and political issues.
